the_planner_cannot_plan_this: scripts/silver/plan_catalog_migration.py + CatalogMigrator.plan_table CANNOT emit this diff today, and that is by design, not a defect: migrate._glue_columns builds the DESIRED table from the contract's `glue_type` -- 'the CURRENT catalog type -- migrations here are additive/property, not the INV-2 widen' (its own docstring) -- so desired == live and plan_table returns NOOP. The sanctioned way to make the planner emit a widen is to move the contract's glue_type to the target FIRST (registry LEADS Glue, the f011_ddl_diff_report._MIGRATION_PENDING mechanism). That registry edit is deliberately NOT taken here: the owner applies the catalog first and the registry is REGENERATED from a re-captured R0 afterwards (the CONAB/tranche-2 apply-then-refresh precedent), so no hand-edited contract ever exists. scripts/ops/pinned_writer_widening_runbook.py builds the desired TableInput from the LIVE table instead, and hands the resulting plan to the SAME CatalogMigrator.apply_table.
partition_projection_note: NOT APPLICABLE and it must stay that way: silver_modis_ndvi is partition_mode `flat` with projection `forbidden`, PartitionKeys is [] and there is no projection.* Parameter. The runbook still asserts PartitionKeys byte-identity ([] before and after) so a future partitioning of this table cannot be smuggled in by a widen. The three table Parameters (EXTERNAL, parquet.compression, transient_lastDdlTime) are carried verbatim. MEASURED PROOF that carrying them verbatim is not paranoia: the 2026-07-15 silver_noaa_oni apply used CatalogMigrator.build_desired_table, whose minimal TableInput dropped Owner ('hadoop' -> None), LastAccessTime, SkewedInfo and BucketColumns and moved NumberOfBuckets -1 -> 0 on that table -- read back live 2026-09-09. This runbook takes the LIVE TableInput verbatim instead and changes only Type tokens.
partition_key_note: There is no partition key on this table to protect. The Hive-style directories under the location (commodity=/country=/region=/year=) are PATH SEGMENTS ONLY: with PartitionKeys [] Athena registers no partitions and reads commodity/country/region/year out of the file body -- which is exactly why `year` is one of the ten body columns being widened here. CatalogMigrator._unsafe_diffs would refuse any partition-key change outright.
coercion_note: AFTER the widen and BEFORE the next canonical promote, the 10,532 existing objects still hold INT32/FLOAT under bigint/double catalog columns. The workgroup that runs every query is `primary` -- the only workgroup in the account (MEASURED 2026-09-09 athena.list_work_groups) -- and athena.get_work_group(WorkGroup='primary')['WorkGroup']['Configuration']['EngineVersion'] reads {'EffectiveEngineVersion': 'Athena engine version 3', 'SelectedEngineVersion': 'AUTO'}, so the reader is engine v3 and its documented Parquet behaviour is to coerce a narrower stored int/float up to the declared wider column. THE IN-ESTATE INSTANCE, and the honest limit of it (see the precedent audit below): reports/silver_readiness/20260712_p65impl/tables/silver_noaa_iod.json records live Glue declaring `double` for dmi_value / iod_dmi_3month_avg / iod_dmi_ethiopia_lag4 while the sampled parquet footer for the same columns reads FLOAT -- a live double-over-float table -- but that footer was captured 2026-07-12 and the object has since been rewritten (s3 head_object 2026-09-05T12:11:36Z), so it is corroboration, not a live proof. NO ATHENA QUERY WAS RUN TO PROVE THIS: the authoring lane is read-only on AWS. The runbook therefore makes the proof the FIRST post-apply step (`--verify-read`, a bounded LIMIT-ed SELECT over the widened columns), and the rollback below restores the narrow types in one restore_table call if it fails. This table's exposure window is the longer of the two (next promote MON 09:00Z), so applying it close to that fire is the cheaper order. WHAT THE PRECEDENTS DO AND DO NOT PROVE, stated exactly (re-verified 2026-09-10): the pink-sheet 'widening' precedent is 44 ADD COLUMNS with no stored type change and therefore carries ZERO coercion evidence; and the 2026-07-15 silver_noaa_oni tinyint->bigint apply does not either, because that table's R0 parquet footer was ALREADY INT64 under a tinyint catalog -- the catalog was catching up to the objects, so no narrow-stored-under-wide-declared read was ever exercised. The ONE real in-estate instance is silver_noaa_iod (R0 tables/silver_noaa_iod.json records physical_type FLOAT for dmi_value / iod_dmi_3month_avg / iod_dmi_ethiopia_lag4 while live Glue declares double today, VersionId 1), and it covers FLOAT->DOUBLE ONLY. SO: the float->double half has an in-estate instance; the int32->bigint half rests on the engine version alone. NO ATHENA QUERY WAS RUN TO PROVE EITHER: the authoring lane is read-only on AWS, so this residual is unavoidable here and is disclosed rather than dressed up. It is BOUNDED, and the bound is the thing that had to be made real: --verify-read is the first post-apply step (a bounded SELECT that now FAILS CLOSED on zero rows, because a missing projected partition returns zero rows without reading a parquet byte), and if it fails the rollback is ONE restore_table call that was MEASURED end-to-end on 2026-09-10 to put all eleven columns back.
sequencing_note: ORDER, and every step's reason. (1) apply this widen (runbook --apply) -- the catalog now leads the objects; (2) prove the existing narrow objects still read (runbook --verify-read) -- if it fails, roll back and stop; (3) let the MON 09:00Z promote fire, or fire the canonical --force-overwrite rewrite by hand: the objects become INT64/DOUBLE and catalog == objects; (4) ONLY THEN re-capture R0 (scripts/silver/run_census.py --table silver_modis_ndvi --check, then --raw) and regenerate (scripts/silver/gen_registry_from_baseline.py --check, then write). STEP 4 MUST NOT RUN BEFORE STEP 3, and this is measured, not cautionary: leviathan.silver.types.classify_drift('int16','bigint') and ('float','double') both return ['glue_catalog_mismatch','widen_*'] (vs [] for ('int64','bigint') and ('double','double')), so an R0 re-capture taken in the window between the ALTER and the rewrite regenerates a contract that still declares widens -- which empties EXPECTED_DEBT but then FAILS tests/unit/silver/test_pinned_writer_catalog_debt.py::test_every_debt_column_is_already_declared_as_an_f062_widen (its second loop asserts a pinned contract off the debt list declares no widen). (5) empty EXPECTED_DEBT to {} and run the decks.
arm_vs_flip_note: There is nothing to arm. No new column, no new partition, no new slug, no producer change -- the producer bytes are already pinned by commit 3f5f4720 and are unchanged by this file. This migration moves TEN catalog type tokens so that the pin the writer already carries becomes legal. It is the DEBT the pin created, being paid.
known_limitation: This widen makes the catalog able to receive the pinned writer's output; it does not make the promote happen, and it does not rewrite a byte. Until the canonical rewrite runs, silver_modis_ndvi is a bigint/double catalog over INT32/FLOAT objects -- the state the coercion_note covers. The rewrite itself is the larger operation of the two families (10,532 objects, 196.2 MB measured 2026-09-09). Also note that the two silver jobdefs must not be repinned past fbe6a7cb until BOTH this and the silver_fgis widen have landed; this file closes one half of that hold, not the hold.
rollback_note: ONE update_table back, through the RESTORE path. The narrow definition is year smallint, period tinyint, pixel_reliability tinyint, and latitude/longitude/ndvi_raw/ndvi/ndvi_z_score/baseline_mean/baseline_std float, with every other field unchanged: `python scripts/ops/pinned_writer_widening_runbook.py --table silver_modis_ndvi --rollback` re-reads live, refuses unless each of the ten is exactly its wide type, asserts Parameters/PartitionKeys byte-identity again, and applies the reverse plan through CatalogMigrator.restore_table. The equivalent DDL is `ALTER TABLE leviathan_dev.silver_modis_ndvi REPLACE COLUMNS (date date, year smallint, period tinyint, commodity string, country string, region string, latitude float, longitude float, ndvi_raw float, ndvi float, pixel_reliability tinyint, ndvi_z_score float, baseline_mean float, baseline_std float, ingest_date string);`. THE ROLLBACK IS NOT apply_table, AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT STYLISTIC. A reverse plan is a NARROWING; leviathan.silver.types.is_narrowing_change returns True for ALL ELEVEN reverse directions across both tables (bigint->int, bigint->smallint, bigint->tinyint, double->float, MEASURED 2026-09-10), and CatalogMigrator.apply_table raises UnsafeMigration on any narrowing. A rollback routed through apply_table would therefore be a DEAD COMMAND -- it refuses, and nothing is restored. --rollback instead goes through CatalogMigrator.restore_table, the sanctioned reverse path (leviathan.silver.types names the precedent in its own comment: B2's F036 int->bigint 'had to detour through restore_table for the same false NARROW'). The narrowing override this represents is BOUNDED: the run refuses unless the unsafe set is EXACTLY the expected NARROW entries for exactly the debt columns -- a DROP, a partition-key change or any other column narrowing still stops it. The restore basis is the LIVE table with only those Type tokens reversed (not the R0 sidecar), so unrelated catalog drift is never reverted; restore_table refuses if the live hash moved since the plan was cut and verifies the post-restore hash itself. MEASURED END TO END 2026-09-10, AWS-FREE: narrow -> --apply -> wide -> --rollback -> narrow against the estate's own in-memory Glue/S3 fakes with a REAL leviathan.silver.lease.Lease, driving the runbook's real apply() -- both directions returned 0, all eleven columns came back to their narrow types, Parameters and PartitionKeys were byte-identical to the pre-apply state (all five projection.* keys plus storage.location.template present), and exactly four update_table calls were issued. The deck test tests/unit/silver/test_pinned_writer_widening_migration.py::test_the_rollback_actually_restores_a_wide_catalog is that round trip. restore_table writes no machine manifest of its own, so the runbook writes a <UTC>_<table>_rollback_restore.json record beside these files carrying the pre-rollback (wide) TableInput as the backup. No parquet object is touched by the apply or by the rollback, in either direction.
